sentences.english: O Lakṣmaṇa! Rāma goes on foot from Ayodhyā to the forest with Sītā to keep the promise of his father.
sentences.devanagari: हे लक्ष्मण रामः पितुः प्रतिज्ञां पालयितुं सीतया सह पद्भ्याम् अयोध्यायाः वनं गच्छति
sentences.iast: he lakṣmaṇa rāmaḥ pituḥ pratijñāṃ pālayituṃ sītayā saha padbhyām ayodhyāyāḥ vanaṃ gacchati

words.why: He is being spoken to (“O …!”); the vocative calls the listener and plays no part in the action.
He does the going: the subject of the active verb “goes”.
The means he travels by: “by (his two) feet”. English “on” is misleading; it is not a place, so not locative.
The place the movement starts from (“from”).
Where a verb of motion ends up: “goes to the forest”. Nothing is done to the forest, so it is not a direct object.
Accompaniment: she goes along with him (सह “with”), not as a tool he uses.
The thing that gets kept: direct object of the infinitive पालयितुम् “to keep”. The purpose is the keeping, not the promise.

alternatives.why: if the purpose is said with a verbal noun, प्रतिज्ञायाः पालनाय “for the keeping of the promise”, the promise is the object of that “-ing” word.

words.why: Possession: it is his father’s promise.

alternatives.why: प्रतिज्ञा “a promising” is itself made from a verb, and the father is the one who promised, so he is also the subject of an “-ing” word.

sentences.english: Sītā says: O Rāma, I go to the forest with you.
sentences.devanagari: सीता वदति हे राम अहं त्वया सह वनं गच्छामि
sentences.iast: sītā vadati he rāma ahaṃ tvayā saha vanaṃ gacchāmi

words.why: She does the saying: subject of the active verb “says”.
Sītā is speaking to him (“O Rāma”).
The one who goes: subject of “go” (गच्छामि, first person to match).
The destination of the verb of motion “go”.
Accompaniment: “with you”, marked by सह.

sentences.english: Rāma goes to the forest, and Lakṣmaṇa too goes to the forest.
sentences.devanagari: रामः वनं गच्छति लक्ष्मणः अपि वनं गच्छति
sentences.iast: rāmaḥ vanaṃ gacchati lakṣmaṇaḥ api vanaṃ gacchati

words.why: Subject of the first “goes”.
Destination of a verb of motion.
Subject of the second “goes”; अपि “too” is indeclinable and changes nothing.
Destination again, the same as for Rāma.

sentences.english: Rāma lives in the forest for fourteen years.
sentences.devanagari: रामः चतुर्दश वर्षाणि वने वसति
sentences.iast: rāmaḥ caturdaśa varṣāṇi vane vasati

words.why: He does the living: subject of the active verb “lives”.
The place where the action happens (“in”).
A number above four works like an adjective with no gender of its own: it agrees with वर्षाणि.

How long the action lasts. Sanskrit treats a stretch of time as the ground an action covers, the way the accusative marks the ground a verb of motion covers, so “for fourteen years” takes the accusative with no preposition.

sentences.english: There is a king named Daśaratha.
sentences.devanagari: अस्ति नृपः दशरथः नाम
sentences.iast: asti nṛpaḥ daśarathaḥ nāma

words.why: Subject of अस्ति “there is”.
A second noun naming the same person as the subject (apposition); नाम “by name” is indeclinable.

sentences.english: That exceedingly righteous king lives happily.
sentences.devanagari: सः अतीव धार्मिकः भूमिपः सुखं जीवति
sentences.iast: saḥ atīva dhārmikaḥ bhūmipaḥ sukhaṃ jīvati

words.why: The pronoun “that” used as an adjective takes its noun’s case.
An adjective modifying the nominative subject.
He does the living: subject of the active verb “lives”.
The neuter singular of सुख “happiness” used as an adverb, “happily”.

sentences.english: “Of the king there is no sorrow,” the people say.
sentences.devanagari: नृपस्य दुःखं न अस्ति इति भाषन्ते जनाः
sentences.iast: nṛpasya duḥkhaṃ na asti iti bhāṣante janāḥ

words.why: Sanskrit has no verb “to have”: “the king has no sorrow” is said “of the king there is no sorrow”.
The thing that (does not) exist: subject of अस्ति “is”.
They do the saying: subject of भाषन्ते “say”.

sentences.english: In that forest lives a Brahmin’s son.
sentences.devanagari: तस्मिन् वने ब्राह्मणस्य पुत्रः वसति
sentences.iast: tasmin vane brāhmaṇasya putraḥ vasati

words.why: The pronoun “that” agrees with वने.
The place where the action happens (“in”).
Possession: the son belongs to the Brahmin.
He does the living: subject of वसति “lives”.

sentences.english: “Ah, I see a beautiful deer!” thinks the king.
sentences.devanagari: अहो सुन्दरं मृगं पश्यामि अहम् इति चिन्तयति नृपः
sentences.iast: aho sundaraṃ mṛgaṃ paśyāmi aham iti cintayati nṛpaḥ

words.why: The one who sees: subject of पश्यामि.
An adjective takes the case of its noun.
What is seen: direct object of “see”.
Subject of चिन्तयति “thinks”.

sentences.english: And he kills the boy with a sharp arrow.
sentences.devanagari: बालकं च तीक्ष्णेन शरेण हन्ति
sentences.iast: bālakaṃ ca tīkṣṇena śareṇa hanti

words.why: The one acted upon: direct object of “kills”.
Agrees with शरेण.
The instrument the action is done with. “With” here means “by means of”, not “together with”.

sentences.english: The Brahmin comes and sees his slain son.
sentences.devanagari: ब्राह्मणः आगच्छति हतं पुत्रं पश्यति च
sentences.iast: brāhmaṇaḥ āgacchati hataṃ putraṃ paśyati ca

words.why: Subject of both verbs, “comes” and “sees”.
The participle “slain” describes the son, so it takes his case.
What is seen: direct object of “sees”.

sentences.english: Because of your wicked deed, I suffer sorrow.
sentences.devanagari: तव दुष्कृतेन अहं दुःखम् अनुभवामि
sentences.iast: tava duṣkṛtena ahaṃ duḥkham anubhavāmi

words.why: Possession: the deed is yours.
The cause or reason: “because of, owing to”.
Subject of अनुभवामि “I suffer”.
What is suffered (literally “experienced”): direct object.

sentences.english: Without my son I do not live.
sentences.devanagari: पुत्रेण विना न जीवामि
sentences.iast: putreṇa vinā na jīvāmi

words.why: विना “without” usually takes the instrumental.

sentences.english: Afflicted by grief, he goes home.
sentences.devanagari: शोकेन पीडितः गृहं गच्छति
sentences.iast: śokena pīḍitaḥ gṛhaṃ gacchati

words.why: The participle describes the unstated subject “he”, so it is nominative.
The agent of the passive participle पीडितः “afflicted”: grief is what afflicts him.

alternatives.why: read as the cause: “afflicted because of grief”.

words.why: Where a verb of motion ends up: “goes home”.

sentences.english: Rāma, jewel among kings, is ever victorious; I worship Rāma, the lord of Ramā; by Rāma the army of night-stalkers was struck down; homage to that Rāma.
sentences.devanagari: रामः राजमणिः सदा विजयते रामं रमेशं भजे रामेण अभिहता निशाचरचमूः रामाय तस्मै नमः
sentences.iast: rāmaḥ rājamaṇiḥ sadā vijayate rāmaṃ rameśaṃ bhaje rāmeṇa abhihatā niśācaracamūḥ rāmāya tasmai namaḥ

words.why: Subject of विजयते “is victorious”. (The verse puts Rāma through every case, one after another.)
A second noun naming the subject (apposition).
Whom I worship: direct object of भजे.
In apposition to रामं, so it takes his case.
The doer of a passive (participle) “was struck down by”.
Subject of a passive verb: the thing the sentence is about, here the one acted upon. The handout lists only the subject of an active verb, but every subject is nominative.
The participle acts as the verb and agrees with what was struck.
नमः “homage” takes the dative: homage to someone.
The pronoun agrees with रामाय.

sentences.english: There is no refuge higher than Rāma; I am Rāma’s servant; may the absorption of my mind always be in Rāma; O Rāma, save me!
sentences.devanagari: रामात् न अस्ति परायणं परतरं रामस्य दासः अस्मि अहं रामे चित्तलयः सदा भवतु मे भोः राम माम् उद्धर
sentences.iast: rāmāt na asti parāyaṇaṃ parataraṃ rāmasya dāsaḥ asmi ahaṃ rāme cittalayaḥ sadā bhavatu me bhoḥ rāma mām uddhara

words.why: Subject of अस्ति “there is”.
An adjective (a comparative) agreeing with परायणं.
With a comparative (“higher than”), the thing compared against is ablative.
Subject of अस्मि “am”.
Possession: the servant belongs to Rāma.
Linked to the subject by “am”: subjective complement, same case as the subject.
Short form of मम “my”: possession.
Subject of भवतु “may it be”.
The object of love or devotion is locative: absorbed in Rāma.
Direct address: “O Rāma”.
Whom he should save: direct object of उद्धर.

sentences.english: But in time he forgets that curse.
sentences.devanagari: किंतु कालेन तं शापं विस्मरति
sentences.iast: kintu kālena taṃ śāpaṃ vismarati

words.why: The instrumental of time passed through: “by the lapse of time, in time”. Whitney gives exactly kālena “in time”.
Agrees with शापं.
What is forgotten: direct object.

sentences.english: He lives happily in Ayodhyā with his wives and rules the kingdom.
sentences.devanagari: अयोध्यायां भार्याभिः सह सुखं वसति राज्यं करोति च
sentences.iast: ayodhyāyāṃ bhāryābhiḥ saha sukhaṃ vasati rājyaṃ karoti ca

words.why: Neuter singular used as an adverb.
The place where he lives (“in”).
Accompaniment with सह “with”.
“Rules the kingdom” is literally “makes the kingdom” (राज्यं करोति): direct object.

sentences.english: So, together with the Brahmins, he performs a sacrifice for offspring.
sentences.devanagari: ततः ब्राह्मणैः सह सः प्रजायै यज्ञं करोति
sentences.iast: tataḥ brāhmaṇaiḥ saha saḥ prajāyai yajñaṃ karoti

words.why: Accompaniment: together with (सह).
Subject of करोति “performs”.
What is performed: direct object.
The purpose of the action: the sacrifice is for getting offspring.

sentences.english: The king’s sons are handsome, calm and heroic.
sentences.devanagari: पार्थिवस्य पुत्राः सुन्दराः शान्ताः वीराः च
sentences.iast: pārthivasya putrāḥ sundarāḥ śāntāḥ vīrāḥ ca

words.why: Possession: the sons belong to the king.
Subject (the verb “are” is understood).
Linked to the subject by an understood “are”: same case as the subject.
Subjective complement, like सुन्दराः.
Subjective complement, like सुन्दराः.

sentences.english: Among them the eldest, Rāma, is the best in virtues.
sentences.devanagari: तेषु ज्येष्ठः रामः गुणैः श्रेष्ठः भवति
sentences.iast: teṣu jyeṣṭhaḥ rāmaḥ guṇaiḥ śreṣṭhaḥ bhavati

words.why: “Among” is one of the locative’s place senses.
An adjective describing the subject Rāma.
Subject of भवति “is”.
Linked to the subject by “is”: subjective complement.
“Best in respect of virtues”, like “by nature”: the instrumental names the respect in which something holds.

sentences.english: Therefore the king loves Rāma especially.
sentences.devanagari: तस्मात् नृपः रामे स्निह्यति विशेषतः
sentences.iast: tasmāt nṛpaḥ rāme snihyati viśeṣataḥ

words.why: Literally “from that”: the cause or reason.
Subject of स्निह्यति “loves”.
The object of love is locative, not accusative.

sentences.english: Whenever Daśaratha sees his eldest son Rāma, he feels supreme joy.
sentences.devanagari: यदा यदा दशरथः ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं रामं पश्यति तदा तदा परमम् आनन्दम् अनुभवति
sentences.iast: yadā yadā daśarathaḥ jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ rāmaṃ paśyati tadā tadā paramam ānandam anubhavati

words.why: Subject of both verbs.
Agrees with पुत्रं.
Whom he sees: direct object.
Names the same person as पुत्रं (apposition), so it takes the same case.
Agrees with आनन्दम्.
What he feels (literally “experiences”): direct object.

sentences.english: Rāma, for his part, is endowed with intelligence.
sentences.devanagari: रामः अपि मत्या युतः
sentences.iast: rāmaḥ api matyā yutaḥ

words.why: Subject (“is” understood).
Linked to the subject by an understood “is”.
युत “joined with” takes the instrumental of accompaniment.

sentences.english: He understands all the Vedas and also goes to the far shore of the science of archery.
sentences.devanagari: सः सर्वान् वेदान् अवगच्छति धनुर्वेदस्य अपि पारं गच्छति
sentences.iast: saḥ sarvān vedān avagacchati dhanurvedasya api pāraṃ gacchati

words.why: Subject of both verbs.
Agrees with वेदान्.
What he understands: direct object.
Where a verb of motion ends up (“goes to the far shore” = masters).
“The far shore of archery”: a relation between two nouns.

sentences.english: One day a certain sage comes to Ayodhyā.
sentences.devanagari: एकदा कश्चन मुनिः अयोध्यां प्रत्यागच्छति
sentences.iast: ekadā kaścana muniḥ ayodhyāṃ pratyāgacchati

words.why: कः + चन “a certain”: a pronoun used as an adjective, agreeing with मुनिः.
Subject of “comes”.
Destination of a verb of motion.

sentences.english: And he speaks to Daśaratha.
sentences.devanagari: दशरथं प्रति वदति च
sentences.iast: daśarathaṃ prati vadati ca

words.why: प्रति “towards, to” takes the accusative.

sentences.english: We sages are sorely tormented by the rākṣasas.
sentences.devanagari: वयं मुनयः राक्षसैः अत्यन्तं पीडिताः भवामः
sentences.iast: vayaṃ munayaḥ rākṣasaiḥ atyantaṃ pīḍitāḥ bhavāmaḥ

words.why: Subject of भवामः “we are”.
Names the same people as “we” (apposition).
Linked to the subject by “are”.
The doer of a passive participle (“tormented by”).

sentences.english: You alone are the protector of the people.
sentences.devanagari: त्वम् एव प्रजानां रक्षकः असि
sentences.iast: tvam eva prajānāṃ rakṣakaḥ asi

words.why: Subject of असि “are”.
Linked to the subject by “are”.
रक्षक “protector” is made from the verb “protect”, and the people are the ones protected: object of a verb-derived noun.

alternatives.why: read loosely as a relation between two nouns, “the people’s protector”.

sentences.english: Who is capable of killing those rākṣasas of whom even the seers are afraid?
sentences.devanagari: येभ्यः राक्षसेभ्यः ऋषयः अपि उद्विजन्ते तेषां हनने कः समर्थः इति
sentences.iast: yebhyaḥ rākṣasebhyaḥ ṛṣayaḥ api udvijante teṣāṃ hanane kaḥ samarthaḥ iti

words.why: Subject (“is” understood).
Linked to the subject by an understood “is”.
“Capable with regard to killing”: the locative of the matter something concerns.
The ones killed: object of the verb-derived noun हनन “killing”.
Verbs of fearing (उद्विजन्ते) take the ablative: what one fears is where the fear comes from.
The relative pronoun agrees with राक्षसेभ्यः.
Subject of उद्विजन्ते “are afraid”.

sentences.english: When Rāma obtains the king’s permission, he goes to the forest with the sage.
sentences.devanagari: यदा नृपस्य अनुज्ञाम् आप्नोति रामः तदा मुनिना सह सः अरण्यं गच्छति
sentences.iast: yadā nṛpasya anujñām āpnoti rāmaḥ tadā muninā saha saḥ araṇyaṃ gacchati

words.why: Subject of आप्नोति “obtains”.
Whose permission: a relation between two nouns.

alternatives.why: अनुज्ञा “permitting” is made from a verb and the king is the one who permits: subject of a verb-derived noun.

words.why: What he obtains: direct object.
Subject of गच्छति “goes”.
Destination of a verb of motion.
Accompaniment with सह.

sentences.english: At that very time many rākṣasas harass those sages.
sentences.devanagari: तस्मिन् एव काले बहवः राक्षसाः तान् मुनीन् बाधन्ते
sentences.iast: tasmin eva kāle bahavaḥ rākṣasāḥ tān munīn bādhante

words.why: Agrees with काले.
The time when the action happens: the locative covers time as well as place.
An adjective agreeing with the subject.
Subject of बाधन्ते “harass”.
Agrees with मुनीन्.
The ones harassed: direct object.

sentences.english: Rāma comes for the protection of the sages from the rākṣasas.
sentences.devanagari: राक्षसेभ्यः मुनीनां रक्षणाय आगच्छति रामः
sentences.iast: rākṣasebhyaḥ munīnāṃ rakṣaṇāya āgacchati rāmaḥ

words.why: Subject of “comes”.
The purpose of coming: “for (the sake of) protecting”.
The ones protected: object of the verb-derived noun रक्षण “protecting”.
Verbs meaning “protect (from)” take the ablative of what one is protected from.

sentences.english: Though only a boy, that hero kills many rākṣasas with his arrows.
sentences.devanagari: बालकः अपि सः वीरः बहून् राक्षसान् इषुभिः हन्ति
sentences.iast: bālakaḥ api saḥ vīraḥ bahūn rākṣasān iṣubhiḥ hanti

words.why: A second noun describing the subject (apposition): “that hero, a boy though he is”.
Pronoun used as an adjective on वीरः.
Subject of हन्ति “kills”.
Agrees with राक्षसान्.
The ones killed: direct object.
The instrument: “with” as “by means of”.

sentences.english: When all the night-stalkers have been killed or have fled, Rāma leaves the forest and comes to Mithilā.
sentences.devanagari: यदा सर्वे निशाचराः हताः निर्गताः वा सन्ति तदा रामः वनं जहाति मिथिलां च आगच्छति
sentences.iast: yadā sarve niśācarāḥ hatāḥ nirgatāḥ vā santi tadā rāmaḥ vanaṃ jahāti mithilāṃ ca āgacchati

words.why: Agrees with the subject निशाचराः.
Subject of सन्ति “are”.
A participle linked to the subject by “are”.
Same construction as हताः.
Subject of both verbs.
What he leaves: direct object of जहाति. Not a destination, though it looks like one.
Destination of “comes”.

sentences.english: Of Janaka there is a most lovely daughter named Sītā.
sentences.devanagari: जनकस्य अतीव रमणीया कन्या सीता नाम
sentences.iast: janakasya atīva ramaṇīyā kanyā sītā nāma

words.why: In place of “to have”: “Janaka has a daughter” is said “of Janaka there is a daughter”.
An adjective agreeing with कन्या.
The one who exists: subject (“there is” understood).
Names the same person as the subject; नाम “by name” is indeclinable.

sentences.english: “She is the best of all women,” people think.
sentences.devanagari: सर्वासां नारीणां श्रेष्ठा सा इति चिन्तयन्ति जनाः
sentences.iast: sarvāsāṃ nārīṇāṃ śreṣṭhā sā iti cintayanti janāḥ

words.why: Subject (“is” understood).
Linked to the subject by an understood “is”.
Agrees with नारीणां.
The group a superlative picks from (“best of”) goes in the genitive: the partitive genitive. The handout lists only possession and the like.
Subject of चिन्तयन्ति “think”.

sentences.english: “I will make a marriage with Sītā,” all the kings think.
sentences.devanagari: सीतया सह विवाहं करोमि इति चिन्तयन्ति सर्वे नृपाः
sentences.iast: sītayā saha vivāhaṃ karomi iti cintayanti sarve nṛpāḥ

words.why: What is made: direct object of करोमि.
Accompaniment with सह: marriage with her. (Natural English “marry Sītā” would hide this.)
Agrees with नृपाः.
Subject of चिन्तयन्ति “think”.

sentences.english: When Rāma saw Sītā, he fell in love with her.
sentences.devanagari: यदा रामः सीताम् अपश्यत् तदा तस्याम् अन्वरज्यत
sentences.iast: yadā rāmaḥ sītām apaśyat tadā tasyām anvarajyata

words.why: Subject of both verbs.
Whom he saw: direct object.
The object of love is locative: “in love with her”.

sentences.english: At that time many kings came for Sītā’s svayaṃvara.
sentences.devanagari: तस्मिन् काले बहवः राजानः सीतायाः स्वयंवराय आगच्छन्
sentences.iast: tasmin kāle bahavaḥ rājānaḥ sītāyāḥ svayaṃvarāya āgacchan

words.why: Agrees with काले.
The time when the action happens.
Agrees with राजानः.
Subject of आगच्छन् “came”.
Whose svayaṃvara: a relation between two nouns.
The purpose of coming: for the bride-choice.

sentences.english: Whatever king fits an arrow on Śiva’s bow, he will marry my daughter.
sentences.devanagari: यः कः अपि राजा शिवस्य चापे बाणं संदधाति सः मम कन्यां परिणयति इति
sentences.iast: yaḥ kaḥ api rājā śivasya cāpe bāṇaṃ sandadhāti saḥ mama kanyāṃ pariṇayati iti

words.why: The relative pronoun agrees with राजा.
कः अपि “any”: agrees with राजा.
Subject of संदधाति “fits”.
What he fits: direct object.
Possession: the bow is Śiva’s.
Where the arrow is set (“on”).
Subject of परिणयति “marries”.
Possession.
Whom he marries: direct object.

sentences.english: Ah, by this easy feat that excellent woman becomes my wife!
sentences.devanagari: अहो एतेन सुलभेन कर्मणा सा उत्तमा नारी मम एव भार्या भवति इति
sentences.iast: aho etena sulabhena karmaṇā sā uttamā nārī mama eva bhāryā bhavati iti

words.why: Agrees with कर्मणा.
Agrees with कर्मणा.
The means by which it comes about: instrument.
Pronoun used as an adjective on नारी.
Agrees with नारी.
Subject of भवति “becomes”.
Possession.
Linked to the subject by “becomes”: same case as the subject.

sentences.english: Not a single king was capable in that feat.
sentences.devanagari: न कश्चन राजा तस्मिन् कर्मणि समर्थः आसीत्
sentences.iast: na kaścana rājā tasmin karmaṇi samarthaḥ āsīt

words.why: With न: “not any”, agreeing with राजा.
Subject of आसीत् “was”.
Linked to the subject by “was”.
Agrees with कर्मणि.
“Capable with regard to that feat”: what the capability concerns.

sentences.english: When Janaka’s daughter was married by Daśaratha’s son, “Well done, well done!” was said by all.
sentences.devanagari: यदा जनकस्य कन्या पर्यणीयत दशरथस्य पुत्रेण तदा साधु साधु इति अभाष्यत सर्वैः
sentences.iast: yadā janakasya kanyā paryaṇīyata daśarathasya putreṇa tadā sādhu sādhu iti abhāṣyata sarvaiḥ

words.why: Possession.
Subject of a passive verb: the thing the sentence is about, here the one acted upon. The handout lists only the subject of an active verb, but every subject is nominative.
Possession.
The doer of the passive verb पर्यणीयत “was married”.
The doers of the passive verb अभाष्यत “was said”.

sentences.english: In time King Daśaratha knows himself to be afflicted by old age.
sentences.devanagari: कालेन राजा दशरथः आत्मानं जरया पीडितं जानाति
sentences.iast: kālena rājā daśarathaḥ ātmānaṃ jarayā pīḍitaṃ jānāti

words.why: The instrumental of time passed through: “by the lapse of time, in time”. Whitney gives exactly kālena “in time”.
Subject of जानाति “knows”.
Names the same person as राजा (apposition).
Whom he knows: direct object.
Linked to the object by an implied “to be”: objective complement.
The doer of the passive participle पीडितं “afflicted by”.

sentences.english: Moreover, he considered his eldest son Rāma fit for the kingship.
sentences.devanagari: अपि च सः स्वस्य ज्येष्ठं पुत्रं रामं राज्ये क्षमम् अमन्यत
sentences.iast: api ca saḥ svasya jyeṣṭhaṃ putraṃ rāmaṃ rājye kṣamam amanyata

words.why: Subject of अमन्यत “considered”.
Possession (स्व “one’s own”).
Agrees with पुत्रं.
Whom he considered: direct object.
Apposition to पुत्रं.
Linked to the object by an implied “to be”: objective complement.
“Fit with regard to the kingship”: what the fitness concerns.

sentences.english: Then the order for Rāma’s consecration was given by the king.
sentences.devanagari: तदा रामस्य अभिषेकाय आज्ञा राज्ञा अदीयत
sentences.iast: tadā rāmasya abhiṣekāya ājñā rājñā adīyata

words.why: Subject of a passive verb: the thing the sentence is about, here the one acted upon. The handout lists only the subject of an active verb, but every subject is nominative.
अभिषेक “consecrating” is made from a verb and Rāma is the one consecrated: object of a verb-derived noun.

alternatives.why: read loosely as “Rāma’s consecration”, a relation between two nouns.

words.why: The purpose of the order: it is for the consecration.
The doer of the passive verb अदीयत “was given”.

sentences.english: From hearing of the consecration, Ayodhyā became as if plunged in an ocean of joy.
sentences.devanagari: अभिषेकस्य श्रवणात् अयोध्या आनन्दस्य सागरे निमग्ना इव अभवत्
sentences.iast: abhiṣekasya śravaṇāt ayodhyā ānandasya sāgare nimagnā iva abhavat

words.why: The cause, “out of, due to”: the joy comes from hearing.
What is heard: object of the verb-derived noun श्रवण “hearing”.
Subject of अभवत् “became”.
Linked to the subject by “became”.
Where she is plunged (“in”).
“An ocean of joy”: a relation between two nouns.

sentences.english: Though delighted by that news, he felt a trace of sorrow.
sentences.devanagari: तेन वचनेन प्रमुदितः अपि सः दुःखस्य लेशम् अन्वभवत्
sentences.iast: tena vacanena pramuditaḥ api saḥ duḥkhasya leśam anvabhavat

words.why: Describes the subject सः.
Agrees with वचनेन.
The cause of his delight: “because of that news”.

alternatives.why: read as the doer of the passive participle प्रमुदितः “delighted by”.

words.why: Subject of अन्वभवत् “felt”.
What he felt (experienced): direct object.
The whole that a part is taken from: “a trace of sorrow” is the partitive genitive. The handout lists only possession and the like.

sentences.english: If the kingdom is ruled by me, then my dear father goes to the forest.
sentences.devanagari: यदि राज्यं मया क्रियते तर्हि प्रियः पिता वनं गच्छति
sentences.iast: yadi rājyaṃ mayā kriyate tarhi priyaḥ pitā vanaṃ gacchati

words.why: Subject of a passive verb: the thing the sentence is about, here the one acted upon. The handout lists only the subject of an active verb, but every subject is nominative.
The doer of the passive verb क्रियते “is done/ruled”.
Agrees with पिता.
Subject of गच्छति “goes”.
Destination of a verb of motion.
